title: Watchdog + ECC spiral triage — daily log
summary: Running day-by-day triage notes for an ECC surge that precipitates watchdog timeouts on a subset of A100 nodes. Contains quick commands, short experiments, hypotheses, and immediate action items for handoff.
content:
Context:
- Incident class: recurring short-lived ECC bursts on particular rack (rack-7), followed within minutes by GPU watchdog timeouts and then node-level kernel panics.
- Affects: small % of serving fleet (3–6 nodes), higher incidence under mixed-workload batching.
- First seen: 2028-09-16 03:20 UTC, reoccurred intermittently through 9/18.

High-level hypothesis (working):
1) Thermal or power transients cause a burst of correctable ECC errors (CEs) on memory rows -> driver tries to recover, increases interrupt/soft-work, which interacts poorly with our watchdog threshold (30s) if combined with heavy KV cache activity.
2) NVLink retry path magnifies latency on PCIe transactions; under sustained CEs the NVLink error-handling stacks cause wedged DMA state and watchdog triggers.
3) After driver attempts and reset, some nodes hit a kernel panic when attempting to remap TLBs while KVM guests are pinned to GPU.

Timeline (selected entries):
- 2028-09-16 03:18 UTC: alert spike — 4 nodes in rack-7 reported CE count > 200 in 10m.
- 2028-09-16 03:22 UTC: first watchdog timeout on node gpu-node-7-12. dmesg shows "GPU watchdog: Resetting GPU" then "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid: 4213".
- 2028-09-16 03:24 UTC: node panics and reboots.
- 2028-09-17 14:03 UTC: repeated pattern during mixed-tenant burst test; observed increased PCIe reset counts on same slot.
- 2028-09-18 01:10 UTC: temporary mitigation applied (lower watchdog timeout to 60s on candidate nodes); observed one prevented panic but next minute CE rate still high.

Immediate findings from quick checks:
- Smart logs: PSU readings around incident show transient +7% voltage dips at 03:18 on host bmc-sensors, concurrent with CE spike (suspected noisy PSU rail).
- Kernel logs: repeated lines: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, 0xbadf00d" (driver-level internal error), then "GPU watchdog timeout".
- ECC histogram: single memory bank (bank 3) accounts for 82% of correctables across samples for the affected nodes — suggests localized DIMM/module problem rather than whole-board thermal.
- NVLink counters: link-retransmit counts ↑ by 3–8x for the duration of CE storm.

Quick diagnostics run (commands run by oncall):
- nvidia-smi memory-errors -i 0 --format=csv
- dmesg | egrep -i "NVRM|watchdog|nvlink|ecc|correctable" --context=2
- ipmitool sensor list | egrep -i "PSU|Voltage|Temp"
- ethtool -S mlx5_core | egrep "link.*error|retransmit"   # for NVSwitch/ethernet fabrics, when applicable
- nvlink --status | grep -A3 Link
(keep outputs attached to JIRA-OPS-4312)

Experiments / temporary mitigations tried:
- Increase watchdog timeout to 90s on two non-critical nodes (gpu-node-7-13, gpu-node-7-15) to allow driver soft-recovery. Result: prevented immediate reboot on 7-13 during the next microburst but CE counts kept rising; 7-15 still hit kernel panic after 40s.
- Offlined suspected DIMM (hot-swap path) via host admin, moved workload away — node stabilized for 12h.
- Bumped NVLink firmware to candidate from staging on one node; telemetry showed reduced retransmit counts but not eliminated CE bursts (suspect correlation, not causation).

Runbook draft (short actionable steps for next oncall):
1) If CE surge detected (CE_rate > 50/min sustained over 2 min):
   - Tag node in monitoring and route traffic away (route policy: canary->fallback)
   - Immediately capture nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,ecc.* --format=csv -l 2 -f /tmp/ecc-sample.csv (10m)
   - Snapshot dmesg (dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg-ecc-$(date +%s).log) and attach to ticket
2) Check PSU / BMC sensor logs for < 5% deviations in +12V or +3.3V rails; if present, escalate to hwops (ticket: HWOPS-PSU-ESCALATE)
3) If CE histogram is concentrated on single memory bank or DIMM and node is in spare window: schedule DIMM replacement or hot-swap; otherwise evict tenants and reprovision to spare pool.
4) If NVLink retransmits > baseline * 3 for >5m: keep node out of rotation and mark for firmware rollback/upgrade trial.
5) Avoid lowering watchdog below 60s except as experimental; prefer routing traffic away.

Outstanding questions / unknowns:
- What is root coupling between PSU micro-transient and ECC bursts? We have one correlated sample but need more telemetry (BMC high-resolution sampling) across incidents.
- Driver path: why does NVLink retransmit escalate CE handling into a watchdog? Need kernel+driver devs to trace NVRM Xid 31 and 79 paths with repro harness.
- Are guest drivers (CUDA contexts in KVM) contributing by holding resources during reset attempts? Need to test with pinned vs non-pinned guests.

Data / telemetry to collect next window:
- High-frequency BMC voltage samples (1s granularity) for rack-7 for next 72h.
- Full ECC per-row dump (nvidia-smi --query-accounting, plus low-level vendor diag) for affected nodes.
- NVLink fabric counters at 1s granularity.
- Correlate tenant scheduling logs (batch windows) to see whether specific batch patterns increase risk.

Action items (owner tags):
- Asha: set up high-frequency BMC sampling for rack-7 (due 2028-09-20).
- Liam: build small repro harness that runs mixed-batch KV cache + synthetic memory touches to try to reproduce CE -> watchdog sequence (due 2028-09-22).
- Marisol: coordinate DIMM replacement window with hwops and inventory (due 2028-09-21).
- Ben: instrument NVLink counters into golden telemetry dashboard (due 2028-09-25).

Handoff notes for next oncall:
- If you see CE spike: do NOT immediately reboot; capture the 10m csv and dmesg first. If node is on critical path, route traffic off before trying resets.
- Firmware experiments are noisy: prefer to do one node at a time. Record exact firmware and driver versions.
- Emergency: if multiple nodes in rack exhibit identical CE bank skew, escalate to hwops immediately (possible chassis-level power issue).

Appendix: useful snippets
- Collect ECC series: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,timestamp,ecc.sbe.volatile,ecc.dbe.volatile --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/ecc-series.csv &
- Print NVLink counters: for i in $(ls /sys/class/infiniband); do cat /sys/class/infiniband/$i/ports/1/counters/port_xmit_data; done  # (example path varies by hw)
- Quick BMC sensor dump: ipmitool -H $BMC -U admin -P $(cat /etc/bmc-pass) sdr elist

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Avoid copy-paste from past playbooks — this sequence feels v different (localized bank + PSU blip).
- Keep documenting each firmware/driver permutation; we need combinatorial coverage matrix.
- If hwops replace DIMM and node stabilizes: capture ECC bank before/after and keep DIMM as suspect so we can test across nodes.

Attachments: (put into linked_artifacts/JIRA-OPS-4312)
- sample-ecc-series-7-12.csv (from 2028-09-16 03:18)
- dmesg-ecc-7-12-20280916.log
- bmc-psu-sample-7-12-20280916.csv

End of log.
